    Problem¶

    rn_forge.web.problem ¶

    RFC 9457 problem details and exception-to-problem mapping.

    No RFC 9457 library is adopted: fastapi-problem 0.12.1 (checked 2026-09-23) emits no instance, sets its own type and title instead of about:blank and the status phrase, and has no exception-to-status registry.

    BLANK_TYPE = 'about:blank' module-attribute ¶

    RFC 9457's prescribed type when there is no type URI to give.

    GENERIC_SERVER_DETAIL = 'An unexpected error occurred.' module-attribute ¶

    What a 5xx detail says when the caller did not supply one. See :meth:ProblemRegistry.build.

    PROBLEM_MEDIA_TYPE = 'application/problem+json' module-attribute ¶

    The Content-Type every error response in this kit carries.

    REQUIRED_FIELD_DETAIL = 'This field is required.' module-attribute ¶

    The detail of a validation error for a missing field, on every stack.

    HasProblemExtensions ¶

    Bases: Protocol

    An exception that contributes extension members to its own problem body.

    :meth:ProblemRegistry.build merges the result beneath an explicit extensions= argument and only for a row below 500 — a 5xx body says nothing about the cause, so nothing an exception carries reaches the wire for one. An application that wants some of AppException.error_data on the wire implements this and chooses the members; error_data itself is never published automatically, since it routinely carries credentials and internal identifiers.

    HasResponseHeaders ¶

    Bases: Protocol

    An exception that contributes response headers to its own problem response.

    :func:render_problem merges the result beneath an explicit headers= argument, so a caller's header always wins a collision.

    ProblemDetail ¶

    Bases: WireModel

    An RFC 9457 problem.

    Extension members are flattened at the top level on the wire (RFC 9457 §3.2): the model allows extra members, and ProblemDetail(..., extensions={...}) merges a mapping in as extras. Core members win a collision with an extension of the same name.

    extensions property ¶

    The extension members, as a fresh mapping.

    as_body() ¶

    Return the wire body, extensions merged at the top level.

    ProblemRegistry(*, type_base='', fallback=INTERNAL_ERROR) ¶

    Maps exception classes to problem types, resolving by MRO.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    type_base str

    Prefix for the type URI. When empty (the default), the type is about:blank, which is what RFC 9457 prescribes when there is no type URI to give — a library must not invent a URI namespace. When set, type becomes type_base + slug.

    		 ''
    fallback ProblemType

    The row an unregistered exception resolves to.

    		 INTERNAL_ERROR

    Example::

    registry = ProblemRegistry(type_base="https://errors.example.com/")
registry.register(OrderLocked, ProblemType("order-locked", 409, "Order Locked"))
body = registry.build(exc, instance="/orders/17").as_body()

    fallback property ¶

    The row an unregistered exception resolves to.

    problem_for(exc) ¶

    Return the row for exc, walking its MRO before falling back.

    The MRO walk is what makes an adapter subclass resolve to its base class's row without anyone remembering to register it.

    problem_for_status(status) ¶

    Return the row for a bare HTTP status that carries no exception type.

    A framework raises HTTP errors no application registered — a routing 404, a 405. The row is the first registered row with that status, so a framework 404 and a LookupError produce the same body. With no such row it is derived from the IANA reason phrase (405 → method-not-allowed / Method Not Allowed); a status with no reason phrase resolves to the fallback.

    register(exc_type, problem) ¶

    Register problem for exc_type, returning self for chaining.

    rows() ¶

    Return a read-only view of the registered rows, in registration order.

    A framework adapter needs the registered exception types — Starlette dispatches a handler per class — and an OpenAPI document needs the statuses they map to.

    type_uri(problem) ¶

    Return the type member for problem.

    ProblemResponse(problem, headers) dataclass ¶

    A rendered problem response, ready for a framework to send.

    The body is :attr:problem's wire form and the Content-Type is always :data:PROBLEM_MEDIA_TYPE.

    body property ¶

    The JSON body, extensions flattened (:meth:ProblemDetail.as_body).

    status property ¶

    The HTTP status.

    ProblemType(slug, status, title) dataclass ¶

    A registry row: the slug, status and title a class of failure maps to.

    default_registry(*, type_base='') ¶

    Return a fresh registry carrying this package's exceptions.

    A factory, never a shared module-level singleton: a consumer that mutated a shared registry would change every other consumer's error bodies.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    type_base str

    Forwarded to :class:ProblemRegistry.

    		 ''

    field_error(path, detail) ¶

    Return one validation-error entry: {"pointer": ..., "detail": ...}.

    The shape is RFC 9457 §3's validation example; a framework binding builds one per field message and puts the list under the errors extension.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    path Iterable[object]

    The field's location, outermost first. Segments are escaped per RFC 6901 §3; an empty path is the document root ("").

    		 required
    detail str

    The human-readable message for that field.

    		 required

    Example::

    field_error(("items", 1, "qty"), "must be > 0")
# {"pointer": "/items/1/qty", "detail": "must be > 0"}

    problem_from_body(status, body) ¶

    Parse an upstream application/problem+json body back into a problem.

    Missing type defaults to about:blank, missing status falls back to status, and unknown members become extensions.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    status int

    The HTTP status of the response the body came from.

    		 required
    body Mapping[str, Any]

    The decoded JSON object.

    		 required

    Returns:

    Type Description
    ProblemDetail

    The parsed problem.

    render_problem(registry, exc, *, instance, problem=None, detail=None, extensions=None, headers=None, realm=None) ¶

    Render exc as a complete problem response: body and headers.

    On top of :meth:ProblemRegistry.build:

    • the current span's trace id is the traceId extension (null when no span is recording);
    • a 401 carries :data:~rn_forge.web.auth.AUTH_FAILED_DETAIL as its detail, whatever detail says, and a WWW-Authenticate challenge unless headers already carries one;
    • when exc implements :class:HasResponseHeaders, its headers are merged beneath headers, so an explicit headers entry wins.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    registry ProblemRegistry

    The rows to render with.

    		 required
    exc BaseException

    The exception being rendered.

    		 required
    instance str

    The instance member — in practice the request path.

    		 required
    problem ProblemType | None

    The row to use instead of resolving one from exc.

    		 None
    detail str | None

    Overrides the derived detail.

    		 None
    extensions Mapping[str, Any] | None

    Extra members, flattened onto the body.

    		 None
    headers Mapping[str, str] | None

    Response headers to carry, e.g. a framework-built challenge.

    		 None
    realm str | None

    The realm of the challenge added to a 401.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    ProblemResponse

    The response. Logging a 5xx is the caller's job.

    unmapped_exceptions(registry, *bases) ¶

    Return every subclass of bases that resolves to registry's fallback.

    Recursively walks __subclasses__() from each base. An application calls this from a test or a readiness check to prove its exception table is total — a domain error that resolves to the fallback becomes a 500 with nothing to catch it.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    registry ProblemRegistry

    The registry to check resolution against.

    		 required
    bases type[BaseException]

    The exception base classes to walk subclasses of.

    		 ()

    Returns:

    Type Description
    list[type[BaseException]]

    The unmapped subclasses, sorted by qualified name.
